$comment: THE ONE FILE FOR MEDIA URLS. See README → 'Adding media'. lectures: one entry per lesson id (YouTube URL or 11-character video id). podcasts: summary episodes; one episode can cover several lessons. Empty strings mean 'not added yet' and the site shows a friendly placeholder. URLs that are not absolute (http/https) are relative to the site root, e.g. test-media/… podcasts[].animatedVideoUrl is the cartoon (animated) version of the same video podcast, a YouTube link, played first when present; animatedPlaylist is its YouTube playlist. The "Player test" episode (test: true) is only built for the browser tests (npm run build:test); showTestEpisodes stays false for the published site.

podcasts.title: Player test (fixture media)
podcasts.description: A 30-second synthetic tone and test pattern bundled with the site so the video and audio players can be checked before the real podcasts are hosted. Not lesson content.

mulebeats.$comment: MuleBeats study songs. Songs are made by hand, reviewed, then set to status "approved" with their audioUrl (a GitHub Release asset, like the podcast MP3s) and real duration. Only approved songs reach the site; planned and review songs are the to-do list. objective (recall-list | process | contrast | concept) and complexity (1-3) choose the genre and target length (src/lib/mulebeats.ts planStyle); genre can be set to override. Songs with test: true exist only in test builds.

tracks.title: Listener, Logger, Database
concepts: HTTP Listener is the source that starts the flow
Logger shows what is happening, even with no business purpose
Database connector Select operation
A dynamic SELECT query, never hard-coded
Transform Message turns the Java result into JSON
Run vs Debug when deploying

tracks.title: Keep the Query Dynamic
concepts: Hard-coded values only ever return one answer
Read the value from the request instead
Then Transform Message from Java to JSON

tracks.title: Run or Debug
concepts: Run deploys the app and just runs it
Debug stops at breakpoints so you can inspect the Mule event

tracks.title: Speak HTTP
concepts: HTTP vs HTTPS: HTTPS encrypts, so a sniffer sees nothing readable
Five core methods: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE
URL anatomy: protocol, host, port, path, query
The rest of a request: params, headers, body, authorization
Response codes and JSON

tracks.title: GET POST PUT PATCH DELETE
concepts: GET reads
POST creates
PUT replaces the whole resource (or creates it)
PATCH changes part of it
DELETE removes it

tracks.title: Lock It with HTTPS
concepts: Plain HTTP can be read by anyone sniffing the network
HTTPS encrypts the traffic

tracks.title: Inside the Mule Event
concepts: The HTTP Listener turns a request into a Mule event
A Mule event carries a message and variables
The message is payload plus attributes
How an HTTP request maps onto the event
The overwrite problem: a new payload replaces the old one

tracks.title: Payload, Attributes, Variables
concepts: Payload: the body, the main data
Attributes: metadata such as headers, query and URI params
Variables: values you keep for later in the flow

tracks.title: Set Variable or Transform Message
concepts: Set Payload / Set Variable set one thing
Transform Message can set the payload and variables in one place
Know which to use and why

tracks.title: Every Folder Has a Job
concepts: Maven gives every Mule 4 project the same structure
src/main/mule holds the flows
src/main/java is rare and fine not to know
src/main/resources holds properties and other files
src/test/munit and src/test/resources are for tests
pom.xml describes the project

tracks.title: Group, Artifact, Version
concepts: POM is the Project Object Model
Identity: group ID, artifact ID, version, packaging
Dependencies and plugins are declared there

tracks.title: A Tour of Anypoint Studio
concepts: Package Explorer on the left
The canvas in the middle
The Mule Palette on the right
Tabs at the bottom
The top menu bar

tracks.title: Console, Problems, Debugger
concepts: Console shows logs and errors
Problems lists what is wrong in the project
Mule Debugger lets you inspect the event step by step
MUnit coverage and errors for tests

tracks.title: Path or Question Mark
concepts: URI parameters identify one exact resource, in the path
Query parameters filter, sort and paginate, after the question mark
The decision rule between them
Strict validation rejects anything not declared

tracks.title: Filter, Sort, Paginate
concepts: Filter narrows the results
Sort orders them
Pagination uses offset and limit

tracks.title: Strict Validation Keeps You Safe
concepts: The misconception: extra parameters are harmless
Strict validation rejects undeclared parameters
Why it matters for security

tracks.title: Call Someone Else's API
concepts: HTTP Listener receives requests; HTTP Request calls out to another API
HTTP Request is how system and process APIs talk in API-led connectivity
Test the third-party API in Postman before touching Mule
Build the flow: listener, request (with the API key), transform
Check the real outgoing request in the debugger
The call's response overwrites the payload

tracks.title: Listener or Request
concepts: The Listener waits for calls coming in
The Request makes a call going out

tracks.title: Shape the Response
concepts: Transform Message builds the final response
Find where each value really sits in the response
Try DataWeave in the Playground first
Kelvin to Celsius: subtract 273.15
Target Variable keeps the original payload
Response Timeout stops a slow call from hanging

tracks.title: Save It in a Target Variable
concepts: Propagation: every call's result replaces the payload
A Target Variable stores the result in a variable instead
So the original payload survives

tracks.title: Don't Wait Forever
concepts: Response Timeout is how long to wait for the other API
Past it, the call fails instead of hanging the flow

tracks.title: Try Again, Then Check
concepts: Reconnection strategy: what to do when the other side is down
Options: Standard (a set number of retries), None, Forever
Response Validator decides which status codes count as success

tracks.title: Standard, None, Forever
concepts: Standard: retry a set number of times, a set time apart
None: fail at once
Forever: keep retrying

tracks.title: One App, Every Environment
concepts: Never hard-code values that change per environment
A property file per environment: .yaml or .properties, no real difference
Configuration Properties global element
Reference properties as ${name}
Pass the environment name at deploy time
Encrypt secrets with Secure Properties

tracks.title: Four Steps to Properties
concepts: Step 1: a property file for each environment
Step 2: a Configuration Properties global element
Step 3: reference the property in each component
Step 4: supply the environment name in the Run/Debug configuration

tracks.title: Keep Secrets Secret
concepts: Sensitive values are encrypted
Secure Properties decrypts them at runtime with a key
The key is supplied at deployment, never stored with the code

tracks.title: When Things Go Wrong
concepts: The default error handler vs your own
Every response, success or error, comes from somewhere you choose
The error object: description and type
On Error Propagate returns an error to the caller
Build a custom error response for each error type
ANY must always go last

tracks.title: ANY Goes Last
concepts: Handlers are checked from the top
ANY matches everything
So specific error types first, ANY at the end

tracks.title: Propagate or Continue
concepts: On Error Propagate: the flow fails and the error goes to the caller
On Error Continue: handle it and return success
Error mapping turns one error type into your own
Three levels: flow, project (global) and component (Try scope)
Raise Error is for business-rule errors
Choice Router routes on a condition

tracks.title: Flow, Global, Try
concepts: Flow-level handlers cover one flow
A global handler covers the whole project
A Try scope handles errors around just a few components

tracks.title: Raise Your Own Error
concepts: Check a business rule with a Choice Router
When it fails, Raise Error with your own type
A handler turns it into the right response

tracks.title: Where Does It Run?
concepts: Four strategies: CloudHub, on-premises, hybrid, Runtime Fabric
Control plane: who provides the management tools
Runtime plane: where the app actually runs
Load balancing and scaling: one server isn't enough

tracks.title: Control Plane, Runtime Plane
concepts: CloudHub: MuleSoft runs both planes
On-premises: you run both
Hybrid: MuleSoft's control plane, your runtime
Runtime Fabric: containers

tracks.title: Life in CloudHub
concepts: CloudHub is integration platform as a service
A worker is the deployment unit
vCore is how workers are sized and billed
Deploy from Runtime Manager, field by field
CloudHub 1.0 vs 2.0
Read the logs in Runtime Manager

tracks.title: Wider or Bigger
concepts: Horizontal scaling: more workers for more requests
Vertical scaling: bigger workers for bigger requests

apps/: drop the app here to deploy
bin/: start and stop the server
conf/wrapper.conf: runtime properties

logs/: system and per-app logs

bin starts and stops

logs records

tracks.title: Hybrid: Their Controls, Your Server
concepts: Hybrid: control plane in Anypoint, runtime on your server
Register the server in three steps
Then deploy to it from Runtime Manager
Troubleshoot patiently, one step at a time
Use the MuleSoft community and meetups
